Chapter 8: Creating Shared Meaning—Building a Life Together.
You know, there’s something powerful about building a life that’s bigger than just you and your partner. Beyond simply managing conflict or handling differences, what really keeps relationships strong over time is this deep sense of shared meaning.
Think of shared meaning as the architecture of your home. Sure, the walls and roof keep you safe, but it’s the little things—your traditions, your values, your inside jokes—that really make it feel like you both belong there. When couples put effort into building this kind of connection, they start to feel a real sense of “us-ness.” All those individual stories and memories get woven together into something larger and more meaningful.
So, how do you actually create shared meaning? Let’s break it down into a few simple, practical steps.
First, you might create family rituals. These are things like regular meals together, holiday traditions, or even a cozy bedtime routine. Little habits like these give you both something to look forward to.
Then, talk about your core values. What truly matters to each of you? And what matters most in your relationship? Getting on the same page about these things helps you feel more connected and united.
Setting shared goals is another big one. Maybe it’s about your careers, maybe it’s family plans, or your personal growth. Working toward something together brings out the best in both of you.
And don’t forget about creating symbols—those reminders of your partnership. That could mean inside jokes, shared hobbies, or even a special object that means something only to you two.
For example, maybe you and your partner decide to have a weekly “date night”—a ritual that helps you reconnect no matter how busy life gets. Or perhaps you start a family tradition of volunteering together every holiday season. These experiences become the glue that holds you together, giving you shared stories and memories to look back on.
It’s also so important to talk about your dreams for the future. Even if your hopes aren’t exactly the same, just sharing them—and supporting each other—can bring you closer. When you both feel like your dreams matter, you’re much more likely to keep investing in your relationship for the long haul.
And here’s something to remember: shared meaning isn’t set in stone. It changes and grows right along with your relationship. By taking time to revisit your rituals, your values, and your goals, you keep things feeling fresh and full of purpose.
So, if you want a partnership that’s more than just surviving—one that truly feels like home—start building a life of shared meaning together. You’ll find that the journey is just as rewarding as the destination.
